newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sets '97 growth, trade, currency targets.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sets '97 growth, trade, currency targets.

text.p: Turkish Finance Minister Abdullatif Sener unveiled the Islamist-led government's 1997 draft budget and economic targets on Friday, setting the trade deficit target at $20.5 billion.
"1997 exports are targeted to stand at $29.5 billion with a 20.4 percent rise (from 1996) and imports at $50 billion with an 11.1 percent increase," Sener told a press conference.
Turkey's 1996 trade deficit target is $16 billion, but senior officials have predicted it would reach more than $20 billion.
Sener said the Gross National Product (GNP) growth rate target was set at four percent for 1997, compared to an expected eight percent in 1996.
The average 1997 dollar rate target was set at 135,000 lira, compared to a 1996 target of 81,250 lira, Sener said.
He said the 1997 GNP deflator target was set at 65 percent, compared to this year's expected GNP deflator of more than 80 percent. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
